comments.text:
The J Craig Venter institute pioneered artificial biological life. They basically learned how to very rapidly sequence genomes and also encode genomes with their own base pair language. We all know A T C G. They used codons which are 3 of the base pairs in a row, so something like ATC, CCC, CTG, etc. They then assigned an alphabet letter to each unique codon and signed their names into the genome, making artificially reproduceable life.

Knowing what the codons do in real life is totally different, and is the subject of this intro. If you look at protein models like Acetylcholinesterase, it looks like a ball of tangled yarn, but when heat is applied or a chemical gradient occurs, the protein moooooves and changes shape, hence the comparison to machines.

comments.text:
"If we could learn to read and write in the code of life, it would make biology programmable."

I'm sure that sounds great and thrilling to programmers and people who have little idea about what's at stake here, and why we should not want this to be accelerated by AI just yet, but this would be yet another technological breakthrough we are far from ready for. Not in the least because even at this stage it is already obvious and certain that it will be used in harmful and stupid ways. Of course it will make shareholders and highly educated, but not all that intelligent scientists very rich and powerful, which seem to be the two main driving forces in our current society. 

And for that reason, humanity needs to first prioritize an inner human evolution (grow up, mature so-to-speak) to get to a much more reasonable level. So far, we are and have been way too destructive, ignorant, and selfish to deal intelligently with what technological advancements offer us. And I am sure we can invent much more for the sake of profit and power, always with the illusion that it will solve our problems, but you can't solve those problems with the same level of awareness and intelligence that created them in the first place. 

That's the perpetual illusion that we keep alive out of ignorance, when the truth is that if we don't evolve beyond our current level of stupidity and ignorance about what's important in life, and how to become better as human beings (and I don't mean technologically enhanced), we are going to keep on suffering the consequences, and make others suffer like we have been doing for so long already. We will just be doing it in new ways and at an ever growing and more dangerous scale. We humans at our current level of awareness and intelligence are the actual source of our problems, and neither AI nor any other technological advancement will solve that problem for us.
